context:
Goal: an undo after a restore never removes a check-in the restore brought back.
Problem (rule): today a Recent row stays live while the card's last-saved time is at or after the row's time. A restore stamps every card with the restore time, so every old row passes. Probe: a count is 1, a row moves it to 2, you restore to 1, and undoing the row sets it to 0.
Based on (record): mailaudit decision recent-checks-can-be-undone: a row is live only while its card still holds the change it describes.
Departs from: recent-checks-can-be-undone, "last-saved time at or after the row's time" — becomes "last-saved time equals the newest log entry on this card" (a), or a stored restore time (b).
Meanwhile: the lane builds a; it fails toward the safe side.
holds: When a mailaudit Recent row can still be undone after a restore.

lastAnswer.note: isnt storing the restore time better

options.gain: A restore, or any write the log did not record, makes old rows read NOTHING TO UNDO.
options.how: A row is live only while the card's last-saved time equals the newest log entry on it.
options.label: Live only while the card's last save is the row's
options.lose: A row can stop being undoable after a sync from a device on an old build.

options.how: The undo log stores when the last restore happened, and rows older than it go inert.
options.label: Store the restore time
options.lose: A new saved field in the app's data.

reply: b is the exact one. Its known cost is one new saved field. I asked the lane at 15:33 CST for anything more: whether a restore or sync from an old-build device breaks b too, and whether a has anything b lacks. If b costs nothing more, the lane builds b, and this item comes back to confirm.
title: mailaudit: after a restore, an undo can remove a check-in the restore brought back. Which test decides a Recent row is still live?
why: An undo that removes restored data loses a check-in you meant to keep.
